title: Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting
classification: Reported observed technique; illustrative attack chain
claim: Microsoft reports MCP tool-poisoning techniques observed against enterprise agents in 2026. The invoice example is illustrative, not a separately verified named-victim breach.
coverage: Native lifecycle/configuration signals are context only. Detecting tool metadata drift requires extra collection not included in the native release. Optional session correlations can identify downstream actions if independently instrumented.

title: Malicious MCP Servers Can Split Instructions to Make AI Coding Agents Exfiltrate Secrets
classification: Research proof of concept; secondary reporting
claim: Controlled testing with fake credentials demonstrated split instructions across MCP metadata and tool responses. It does not establish malicious intrusions or real-world success rates.
coverage: Optional session-level injection and data-submission correlations only; native process/network signals cannot prove secret-file reads or detect the split instructions themselves.

title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
classification: Observed malicious credential abuse; adversarial use of AI
claim: Microsoft reports agentic discovery and abuse of exposed credentials, followed by cloud access. This is not evidence of prompt injection against a victim AI agent.
coverage: Known agent service-principal permission and sign-in anomalies are partial coverage. This release does not inventory arbitrary stolen AI API keys, collect Key Vault data access by default, or prove resource exfiltration from sign-ins.
actorAttribution: No additional attribution inferred by this content pack
